races.name: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Dream Illusion
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good recently and travels prominently — Michael Herrington's filly has strong place form at this trip on similar ground and is well-drawn to slot in behind the leader; 34 days off is not a concern for this yard's 3/15 strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Dream Illusion was a solid second last time out and has form figures including a win in her last six starts, with today's trip and going both proven. Our rating of 72 puts her only fourth of eight, the one blot against an otherwise consistent profile.

runners_data.name: Ironist
runners_data.note: George Margarson's mare returns quickly on nine days' rest and has placed twice in seven good-ground runs, tracking pace naturally over this exact trip; the 5lb claimer Mason Paetel is a marginal negative but the style and trip fit is strong.
runners_data.comment: Ironist has been workmanlike rather than eye-catching, with only a third to show from her last five starts, but a strong speed figure of 75 hints at more ability than the bare positions suggest. Both trip and going are proven, though she dipped to a below-par eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Izzy Fast
runners_data.note: Philip McBride's filly holds up in rear and won over six furlongs on good ground last time — stepping up to seven requires a stronger gallop than Lovers Leap is likely to provide, which is the key risk; Hector Crouch is a reliable partner if she can find cover early.
runners_data.comment: Izzy Fast managed just one win from her last five starts and faded to seventh last time out, though she is proven over today's trip and going. Our rating of 66 rates her only seventh of eight, and a 41-day absence adds to the questions.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Consistently placed in sprint handicaps and wears a hood — Michael Appleby sends this one in genuinely wanting to race from off the pace, but she has been placed at the rear of the midfield map because the field has too many hold-up types for all to find their natural position; a soft pace will blunt her chance markedly.
runners_data.comment: Fantasy Obsessor has been a model of consistency, runner-up three times in her last six starts, with both trip and going proven and first-time cheekpieces added. Our rating of 73 puts her second of eight, though the stable is out of form at just 5% recently.

runners_data.name: Lovers Leap
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's sole confirmed front-runner and the pivot of this entire race shape — Billy Loughnane should face no challenge for the lead, and while her OR-70 makes her the top weight, one win and one place from two runs on good ground underpin the profile; 46 days off bears monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Lovers Leap boasts a win in her last five starts and has never finished worse than sixth in that time, with both today's trip and going fully proven. Top of our figures at 77, she rates the one to beat, with only a 46-day absence to note.

runners_data.name: Angels' Share
runners_data.note: William Knight's filly has a win over seven furlongs on standard ground but has run poorly in her last three, all finishing eighth or worse; Cieren Fallon adds class in the saddle and she is a hold-up type who needs a genuine pace test she may not receive here.
runners_data.comment: Angels' Share won earlier in this sequence of starts but has managed nothing better than eighth since, including last time out. She does arrive with both today's trip and going proven, and our rating of 72 places her a fair fifth of eight.

runners_data.name: Allegrino
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's consistent three-year-old has placed in five of six starts and prefers to race prominently — William Buick's presence is a major positive, and while he has been mapped to midfield due to positional congestion up front, his natural instinct will be to push forward; STYLE_FIT flag suggests a modest discount if he cannot recover his position.
runners_data.comment: Allegrino has been admirably consistent, never out of the first three in five starts including a win, with today's distance in her favour. Yet our rating of 65 is the softest in this field, leaving her only eighth of eight.

runners_data.name: Galileo Charm
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's filly has won and placed over this exact trip on a sound surface and is another true prominent runner displaced to midfield by the field's pace composition — Robert Havlin will likely push forward early, and 50 days off over seven furlongs on good-to-firm are the key variables to weigh; STYLE_FIT flag applies if the front becomes congested.
runners_data.comment: Galileo Charm won earlier in this six-race sequence and was frequently competitive around it, but her last two starts have both ended in seventh. Today's distance is proven, and first-time cheekpieces are added, with our rating of 68 placing her a middling sixth of eight.

races.paceDynamic: Lovers Leap is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Billy Loughnane should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front on good-to-firm ground over seven furlongs at Yarmouth's flat, straight track. The pace is unlikely to be searingly fast, which means the race will be run at a sustainable rhythm that compresses the finish rather than blowing it apart — a scenario that rewards horses racing close to the pace rather than those needing a strong end-to-end gallop to close into. Dream Illusion and Ironist sit naturally prominent and are best placed to capitalise behind the leader, while Allegrino and Galileo Charm are true prominent types shuffled into a midfield mapping because this field carries more pace horses than the race shape can accommodate — Lovers Leap and Dream Illusion are most likely to actually command the forward positions. This race shape strongly favours prominent/close-to-pace runners who can latch onto the leader early and quicken in the straight, as genuine hold-up horses will find insufficient pace to generate a true late run on this flat, forgiving track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lovers Leap Leads, Front Pair Win
scenarios.trigger: If Lovers Leap trots up unchallenged early and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop, allowing the horses immediately behind to travel with minimal effort.
scenarios.body: Lovers Leap dictates from the front and the race develops into a tight-knit group arriving at the two-furlong pole together, whereupon the horses who tracked the leader throughout have the positional advantage and stamina to quicken on good-to-firm ground. Dream Illusion and Ironist, both natural prominent racers suited to this trip and going, are ideally placed to strike.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Redistribution Shakes Up Front
scenarios.trigger: If Allegrino or Galileo Charm pushes forward early despite their midfield mapping and contests the pace, creating a mildly contested but still manageable tempo.
scenarios.body: A slightly quicker early pace stretches the field fractionally but still does not generate enough of a true test for hold-up horses to close, leaving the winner likely to emerge from the top four or five throughout. Allegrino's consistent placed form on similar ground and William Buick's positional intelligence make him a serious threat if he can recover his natural prominent berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves deceptively brisk and the front-runners tie each other up, allowing a gap to open in the straight for closers.
scenarios.body: Izzy Fast, who has won over six furlongs on good ground and carries hold-up credentials, and Angels' Share, with her winning form at seven furlongs on a sound surface, would be the primary beneficiaries of a late collapse in the leaders. This scenario is discounted because Fantasy Obsessor and Angels' Share are genuine hold-up types but depend on a pace they are unlikely to receive in a one-paced lead scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses contest the early lead aggressively and the race breaks into small groups, creating an uneven gallop that scrambles typical pace shapes.
scenarios.body: A muddling pace and fractured field pattern can produce a surprise result from any position, and Fantasy Obsessor's consistency in placed efforts suggests she could be found close enough if the race falls apart tactically. Galileo Charm's winning experience over seven furlongs on a sound surface gives her an outside claims if the pace suits unexpectedly.

watchPoints.text: Lovers Leap — if Billy Loughnane is allowed to dictate a soft, uncontested gallop, the entire field's pace profile is compromised; watch whether any of Allegrino or Galileo Charm pushes to challenge her early, as their natural style means Buick and Havlin may not accept a midfield role.

Allegrino and Galileo Charm are both mapped to midfield but are genuine front-runners by style — if they push forward and compress the early lead group, the race tempo becomes harder to predict and the hold-up horses gain a marginal opportunity they otherwise lack.

Izzy Fast's win last time was over six furlongs — the step up to seven on a flat track with a likely moderate pace is a significant ask; watch whether Hector Crouch settles her early or rides her more prominently than her hold-up profile suggests.

Fantasy Obsessor has shown consistent placed form at shorter distances and wears a hood — if the hood sharpens her early, she may find herself closer to the pace than her hold-up profile implies, which could be a positive or expose her to a stint she does not want.

Angels' Share has not won on turf good going and has finished eighth or worse in her last three — Cieren Fallon's booking is eye-catching given the poor recent form, and any market move in her direction on track should be noted before the off.

races.name: Infobond Nursery

runners_data.name: Dubai Charm
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's improving filly has placed twice at 6f on Good, suggesting she handles this surface well at a shorter trip, and Billy Loughnane is well-placed to pounce from off the pace if the pace eases in the closing stages; 19 days since last run is routine.
runners_data.comment: Dubai Charm brings strong clock figures into this race, a speed rating of 78 underpinning our rating of 81, good enough for second of eight. She was placed twice before an unplaced effort last time out, with the yard out of form at just 4% recently.

runners_data.name: Fly Test
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on this Michael Bell runner who has placed once in three starts at 5-6f on Good, but the flagged fade in the finish is a real concern on this flat, unrelenting track where there is nowhere to hide in the final furlong.
runners_data.comment: Fly Test bounced back with a solid second last time out, having found little in a below-par eighth and an unplaced effort before that. Both today's trip and going are proven, and our rating of 74 puts him a competitive fourth of eight, fresh just 13 days on.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and last-time-out winner over this exact 5f Good trip, giving her an obvious tactical advantage; Stuart Williams keeps her fresh on a 6-day turnaround and Buick's presence amplifies her chance of dictating terms, though her STYLE_FIT tag slightly tempers the ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Holi Scarlett arrives in fine form, winning last time out just six days ago to cap a progressive sequence. Both today's trip and going are proven, and a strong speed rating of 73 backs our rating of 75, third of eight, though the yard is out of form of late.

runners_data.name: Or Another
runners_data.note: K R Burke's gelding showed solid form finishing third and fourth over 5f on Good, and visor headgear adds a variable; a true hold-up horse by nature, pushed into mid-division on the map because the field's closing contingent is large — 42 days off is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Or Another managed a fourth last time but is without a win in a short recent spell. Both today's trip and going are proven, though our rating of 70 is only seventh of eight, and a 42-day absence adds to the questions.

runners_data.name: Sable Island
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's filly has placed twice at 6f but her one run at 5f saw her finish seventh, making the trip a mild query; a genuine hold-up type by style, her race position on the map reflects overcrowding at the rear rather than her natural inclination, and hood headgear is noted.
runners_data.comment: Our rating of 88 puts Sable Island clear of this line-up, despite finishing outside the frame just once in three runs this spell, with two thirds among them. Today's distance is proven, though a modest speed figure of 64 and being without a win in that time offer one note of caution.

runners_data.name: My Maria
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's lightly-raced filly is flagged as having an unknown style, having run just twice, and represents the most intriguing unknown quantity in the field; she handles Good ground and Kieran Shoemark is an intelligent booking, but two runs of evidence makes her hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: My Maria has been competitive without breaking through, a fair third last time out, and remains without a win in a short recent spell. Today's distance is proven, and our rating of 71 rates her a fair fifth of eight, back after a 32-day gap.

runners_data.name: Cydney Sweenie
runners_data.note: Jack Morland's filly has struggled for consistency — an 8th at 6f followed by a third and a fourth — and her trainer has had no winners in the past 14 days; a natural closer whose actual race position will be further back than the map implies, and the absence of a strong pace to close into is a genuine tactical problem.
runners_data.comment: Cydney Sweenie disappointed when eighth last time, having shown more with a third and fourth earlier, and remains without a win in that spell. Today's distance is proven, but our rating of 62 is the softest here, leaving her eighth of eight after a 43-day absence.

runners_data.name: Miss U Gino
runners_data.note: Philip McBride's filly has failed to land a blow in three starts with two 10th-place finishes, the fade-in-finish flag is a serious concern, and she is a genuine hold-up runner whose chances are significantly undermined by the race's likely lack of end-to-end pace to close into.
runners_data.comment: Miss U Gino's finishing positions have been modest of late, no better than fifth in her last three starts, without a win in that time. Both today's trip and going are proven, and our rating of 70 sits well above her official mark of 57, hinting at more to come.

races.paceDynamic: Holi Scarlett is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Yarmouth nursery and, on Good to Firm ground with William Buick aboard, she is likely to dictate an uncontested, metronomic gallop from the outset. Behind her, the field is dominated by hold-up types — Or Another, Sable Island, Cydney Sweenie and Miss U Gino are all true closers who cannot all occupy their natural rear position and have been redistributed toward midfield on the map. With no genuine pace rival to push Holi Scarlett into a fast early split, the tempo is likely to be controlled rather than burning, which compresses the race and reduces the premium on a late run. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or within a length or two of the leader from halfway, as the absence of a strong early pace makes a winning late swoop from the back considerably harder to execute.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Holi Scarlett Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Holi Scarlett gets away cleanly and is allowed to dictate a comfortable, uncontested tempo throughout
scenarios.body: Buick settles Holi Scarlett on the front end with no rival willing or able to pressurise her, and the race becomes a test of straightforward cruising speed rather than finishing kick. Her recent win at 5f on Good suggests she stays well within herself when allowed this luxury, and the hold-up horses behind face too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leaders Late
scenarios.trigger: If Holi Scarlett's advantage shrinks in the final furlong and a well-positioned hold-up horse finds a decisive late gear
scenarios.body: This only materialises if Holi Scarlett has overcautiously been allowed to bowl along and the pace is fractionally stronger than it appears, leaving her exposed in the last 100 yards. Dubai Charm and Or Another, both with respectable form on similar going, are the most naturally suited closers if this shape emerges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at an even gallop and a horse tracking in second or third position produces a decisive burst turning into the straight
scenarios.body: With several hold-up horses redistributed into midfield, any of them travelling strongly at halfway could find themselves in a position to challenge without needing a true closing run. My Maria and Or Another, both lightly raced and unexposed, carry potential for improvement and could exploit a pitch-and-run scenario from mid-division.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Upset — Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically and a lightly-raced or overlooked runner benefits from chaos or a badly-run affair
scenarios.body: Miss U Gino and Cydney Sweenie both hold modest credentials and form figures that do not inspire, but in a messy scenario where jostling from the redistributed hold-up pack disrupts running lanes, an unconsidered runner could sneak through. This scenario is low probability given the straightforward nature of the race shape.

watchPoints.text: Holi Scarlett — if William Buick gets a clean break and she leads unchallenged past the two-furlong pole, the hold-up horses redistributed into midfield may lack the sprint to reel her in on this flat, fast 5f track.

Or Another and Cydney Sweenie — both are true closers mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; watch whether they actually settle mid-division in running or drift further back, because if they end up in their natural position they face a very stiff ask against a front-runner in a soft pace.

Fly Test — the flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a significant concern at Yarmouth's unforgiving straight 5f on Good to Firm ground; if she is held up and the pace does not truly test the leaders, her chance evaporates quickly.

My Maria — Archie Watson's unknown-style runner with just two career starts could behave unpredictably in terms of positioning; watch the early-race footage to see whether Shoemark chooses to hold her up or push forward, as that will define which scenario she participates in.

races.name: ATI Tank Hire Memorial Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Raneem
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly already has a win over 7f on Good ground to her name and steps up to a mile here, a trip her pedigree should embrace; she tracks up naturally in a prominent position and, with only four runners, is well-placed to stalk Starlight Lass and pounce — Ray Dawson's booking for a Varian runner commands attention.

runners_data.name: Starlight Lass
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter, trained by the powerful Gosden team and returning just 12 days after a win at a mile on Good ground, which is an ideal preparation; she takes control from the front but, racing essentially in her natural lead role in a race that may not pressure her, she sets the terms — the question is whether she has a finishing kick when joined.

runners_data.name: Dream Vega
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly is a natural front-runner by disposition yet finds herself unable to secure the lead with Starlight Lass in the field; her two runs have both been in the 4-7 range on Good ground over 7f, and the step to a mile on fast ground is an open question — her chance is modestly discounted by the fact she is racing behind where she wants to be.

runners_data.name: Sakura Impact
runners_data.note: A debutante with no form to assess, shown at the rear of the map simply because the field is light on true hold-up types; trainer Mrs Gansera-Leveque has had only one runner in the past 14 days and the apprentice booking of Harry Burns (3) adds further uncertainty — treat with caution until her natural style and ability are established.

races.paceDynamic: Starlight Lass is the confirmed front-runner and, with only four runners on a flat mile at Yarmouth in Good to Firm conditions, she is likely to stride out unopposed from the front and set a sustainable, even gallop rather than a pressured one. Raneem and Dream Vega are both natural prominent types, but with Starlight Lass already owning that lead role, at least one of them will be forced to settle closer to midfield than ideal — Dream Vega in particular has been redistributed to a mapped midfield position because the field cannot accommodate every prominent horse at the front simultaneously. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position, and Starlight Lass is most likely to take the true lead with Raneem the likelier of the two remaining prominents to slot just behind her. A steady, uncontested pace on a flat track in fast conditions classically rewards horses who travel well in a prominent position and quicken from two furlongs out — the profile that benefits most here is the close-tracking, prominent racer who can respond to a sustained gallop rather than a sharp injection of pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Prominent Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If Starlight Lass sets an uncontested, even pace and the race is decided by a sustained finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Starlight Lass bowls along in front at a comfortable clip, and the horse tracking closest into the straight has first run on the field; with no pace injection to disrupt rhythm, whoever travels smoothly in second or third has the race at their mercy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Starlight Lass finds extra reserves when challenged and simply outstays her rivals on the fast ground over the full mile.
scenarios.body: Starlight Lass controls every yard of the race and, when asked to quicken inside the final two furlongs, finds enough to hold every challenger; a true galloper's finish on Good to Firm ground suits a horse who has already led throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a sustained run from behind and a hold-up horse finishes powerfully.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because the only genuine hold-up type, Sakura Impact, is unknown in form and has been redistributed to the rear simply to fill that map position; Dream Vega, mapped to midfield, is also a natural prominent type racing out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint finish with no true rhythm established.
scenarios.body: An unusually slow tempo with four runners could produce a sprint-style finish from the two-furlong marker, but the presence of a confirmed front-runner in Starlight Lass makes a genuine slow-burn scenario very unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Raneem travels smoothly in Starlight Lass's slipstream — if she tracks the leader without being asked, she will have first run on the field entering the final two furlongs and becomes the most dangerous closer in this shape.

Starlight Lass's settling behaviour in the early stages is critical; if she is allowed to bowl along at her own pace she could be very hard to peg back, but any sign of pulling or racing keenly over the first two furlongs could drain her reserves on a flat, fast mile.

Dream Vega's tactical position in the early stages deserves monitoring — if Kieran Shoemark elects to push forward regardless and challenge Starlight Lass for the lead, the resulting pace increase could fundamentally alter the race shape and open it up for late runners.

Sakura Impact is an unknown quantity on debut; watch her odds movements and her initial jumping behaviour — any significant market support or a clean, composed start would upgrade her from a pure speculative runner to a factor worth tracking into the straight.

The Good to Firm ground confirmed for the 3:15 at Yarmouth slightly upgrades the speed premium in this race — horses who have already shown they handle fast conditions (Raneem and Starlight Lass both have such form) carry an edge over those facing it for the first time.

races.name: Great Yarmouth Racecourse Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ancestor
runners_data.note: Lightly raced William Haggas three-year-old with just one run — a fourth at 10f on good — making it genuinely hard to assess style or ceiling, but the stable and Cieren Fallon partnership at this level commands respect; OR of 120 says connections see serious potential.

runners_data.name: Kokbastau
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's two-year-old (as rated) returning after a lengthy 292-day absence following a sole run — a sixth on soft ground over 8f — meaning the step up to 1m2f on good-to-firm and the layoff both need answering before this can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Traveling Man
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes hold-up type who has placed twice in two starts at 10f including on good ground, giving him solid form pointers for this trip and surface; Ray Dawson's booking is modest but the horse's profile suits a steadily-run race where he can close into a sprint.

runners_data.name: Waterford Castle
runners_data.note: George Boughey's consistent performer has placed in five of six career starts, running consistently at this trip on good ground; Billy Loughnane takes the ride and the horse wears a hood — though as a true hold-up type placed into midfield by the race shape, his finishing kick may not be fully deployed here.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old showed placed form last time at 10f on good ground with William Buick — the stable's leading jockey — retaining the ride, which is a positive; like Waterford Castle, this is a genuine hold-up horse that the race shape is likely to push forward against its natural inclinations, tempering its claims.

runners_data.name: Seacole
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's lightly raced filly ran a promising second on her only start at 10f on good ground and wears headgear (hood); Beckett's 14-day strike rate of 8/58 is solid, and an OR of 120 alongside Hector Crouch's booking makes this one of the more interesting runners despite the stylistic unknown.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m2f maiden on good-to-firm ground at Yarmouth shapes up as a slowly-run, tactical affair where the pace is likely to be dawdled before a sprint finish from around the two-furlong pole. Ancestor and Seacole are both unproven stylistically, while Kokbastau, Traveling Man, Waterford Castle, and Hollywell Stream all carry hold-up profiles — meaning the field is loaded with horses that want to be covered up, and the collective reluctance to lead will compress the race into a late dash. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear, and Waterford Castle and Hollywell Stream are most likely to be shuffled forward into midfield by the race's natural flow. This race shape — a slowly-run, bunched sprint finish — strongly favours horses with a high cruising speed and a sharp turn of foot over the final two furlongs, making runners with strong recent form on similar good ground who can quicken from a stalking position the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bunched Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls through the first mile and the race degenerates into a straight-line sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: All six runners are in contention turning in with minimal gaps, and the race becomes a flat-out dash to the line; horses with the highest peak speed and tactical sharpness thrive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Gallop, Class Tells
scenarios.trigger: If an honest but unspectacular gallop is set from the front and the race is run at a consistent tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: A moderate but even pace allows the classier horses to sustain their effort and pull clear from two furlongs out without a sudden brutal sprint; horses who stay the trip well and have shown ability in similar conditions benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Pinches It
scenarios.trigger: If Ancestor or Seacole, racing with unknown or front-running tendencies, takes the initiative and dictates from the front at a comfortable pace.
scenarios.body: Dictating on a flat, fair track at Yarmouth on good-to-firm ground can be very potent when no rival has the inclination or instructions to challenge; a horse that steals a march on a hold-up heavy field could build an unassailable advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early and the two redistributed hold-up types — Waterford Castle and Hollywell Stream — manage to secure their natural rearward position and produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Waterford Castle's consistent placed form at this trip on good ground gives her a genuine chance if she gets cover and a strong pace develops; Hollywell Stream showed ability last time when placed on identical going and could benefit from a truly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Seacole and Ancestor are both OR 120 unknowns with lightly-raced tags — if either takes up the running unchallenged, the hold-up heavy field has no natural rival to go with them.

Waterford Castle and Hollywell Stream are true hold-up horses that this race shape will push into midfield; watch for either being unable to drop in and losing their customary cover, which would compromise their chance significantly.

Kokbastau returns after 292 days off for Roger Varian — watch the market for any significant support, as Varian's string often come fit first time back but the soft-ground form and jump to 1m2f on good-to-firm is a live concern.

With no front-runner, watch the early stages closely — if the field crawls to the home straight, the entire race will be decided in the final two furlongs and draw and position off the bend will matter more than form.

races.name: Marine Lodge Handicap

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: Course-effective hold-up performer with strong recent form (1-2-3 in last three applicable starts) who has genuine winning ability on similar Good ground; only one day since last run is worth noting but she has been busy all season and her sim-going record of 1W3P from six runs is the standout strike-rate in this field — her natural style keeps her closest to the map position the race shape rewards.
runners_data.comment: One win in her last six starts, including a second last time out, and rushed back within a day; already proven over today's trip and going, she tops our figures and rates the one to beat, with the quick turnaround the only query.

runners_data.name: Regal Guest
runners_data.note: 41 days off the track for Margarson's yard which has shown zero wins from 11 runners in the past fortnight; his sim-going record is a bare 0W0P from four efforts and his recent form figures of 7-6-10-5-7 suggest he is struggling to land a blow at this level — a hold-up type who needs a stronger gallop than Charlatan is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time cheekpieces for this reappearance after 41 days off, and proven over today's trip and going, he ranks third on our figures and remains capable of running into the frame; winless in his last five starts, the extended layoff is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Charlatan
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here who should dictate terms unopposed, but his Simulated-going record of just 1 win from 15 runs on comparable ground is uninspiring, and a STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 flags he is being asked to lead when his best form has come from a prominent but not pace-making role — he sets the shape without necessarily winning it.
runners_data.comment: Proven over today's trip and going and with a second among his recent finishes, he cannot be dismissed on figures alone; but he is winless in his last five starts and having his first run in 41 days, form and fitness are the questions he must answer.

runners_data.name: Bizarre Law
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Soft for Herrington recently and has placed form on Good ground; naturally a hold-up type who has been remapped closer to the pace because the field is saturated with closers, meaning he cannot produce his trademark deep finish — the style displacement (STYLE_FIT 0.91) tempers confidence even though the trainer has shown some recent form at 3/18 over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back confirms he retains ability, and he steps up in first-time cheekpieces back within 24 days of his latest run; second-best on our figures here, he rates a live threat, with modest placings either side of that win the only slight caveat.

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: The most proven performer on similar ground in this field with 2W2P from 10 sim-going runs, and she carries headgear without listed change; at age eight she is an experienced hold-up type forced to race from a position closer than suits her, robbing her of the late punch that earned those wins — the discrepancy between her best form and her likely race position is the key risk factor here.
runners_data.comment: A second last time out is the one bright spot in a modest sequence that also features three finishes outside the frame; without a win in her last five starts and toward the bottom of our rankings here, she needs more than recent placings suggest she has to figure.

runners_data.name: Rokuni
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a poor recent profile of 0s and 9s, 0W0P from nine sim-going runs, and a headgear note of tongue-tie and visor flagging trainer experimentation; Christian Howarth (3) takes the ride but the raw form makes this the weakest profile in the field, and being a true hold-up type squeezed into a midfield position further reduces the already slim prospect of a notable finish.
runners_data.comment: Three unplaced efforts fill out a sequence with nothing better than sixth, leaving him rock-bottom on our figures; the first-time tongue-tie and visor, and a quick reappearance after just 12 days, are the only reasons for cautious interest, but he remains difficult to fancy on the form shown.

races.paceDynamic: Charlatan is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him, he should be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Yarmouth's straight mile on Good to Firm ground. The remainder of the field — Prefer The Sister, Regal Guest, Bizarre Law, Heer's Sadie, and Rokuni — are all natural hold-up or prominent types, meaning the pace Charlatan sets will not be pressured and the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching. This field holds considerably more hold-up runners than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Bizarre Law, Heer's Sadie, and Rokuni are all genuine closers but will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would prefer, compromising their ability to produce a true late surge. A single, uncontested pace-setter on fast ground over a straight mile strongly favours a horse with the tactical speed to track Charlatan's controlled gallop from a prominent position and quicken past him in the final two furlongs — positional racers who can sit second or third will be best placed, not the deep hold-up horses who lose their best weapon when the pace is moderate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Charlatan Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Charlatan bowls along at a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the field fails to produce a sustained early challenge.
scenarios.body: Charlatan sets a measured pace that keeps the race well within himself, and a horse positioned just behind him in second or third can track him through and pounce in the closing stages without needing to make up ground from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positions itself just off Charlatan's shoulder and produces a decisive turn of foot inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The controlled tempo set by Charlatan means there is enough petrol left in the tank for a well-placed tracker, and the straight Yarmouth mile rewards horses who can quicken from a handy position rather than those making up ground from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Charlatan's controlled pace is slightly faster than it appears and he ties up near the furlong pole, allowing the hold-up brigade to arrive late.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Charlatan to have set enough pace to come back to the field, which is less likely given there is no rival to force him beyond his comfort zone; the redistributed hold-up horses — Bizarre Law, Heer's Sadie, Rokuni — would need to find their natural closing run from positions closer than ideal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Charlatan crawls to such an extent that the race becomes a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow pace compresses the field and turns the race into a dash for home, in which case the highest-rated horse with the best turn of foot in the final stages benefits most regardless of running style.

watchPoints.text: Charlatan (Muscutt) setting a deceptively slow pace — if he crawls early the race bunches and his STYLE_FIT tag means he may not have the finishing kick to hold on when the field arrives.

Bizarre Law, Heer's Sadie, and Rokuni are all natural closers forced to race closer to the pace than ideal — watch whether any of them get trapped in a pocket or waste energy fighting for position in the early stages.
Prefer The Sister ran only yesterday (LR: 1d) — monitor market moves and paddock demeanour for any signs of fatigue or below-par condition that the bare form string would not yet reflect.

Regal Guest returns after 41 days off for a trainer showing 0 wins from 11 runners in the past fortnight — a combination of fitness doubt and poor strike-rate makes his price the most likely to drift in the ring.

Good to Firm ground confirmed for this race (despite the declared Going of Good in the header) — the faster surface marginally increases the advantage of a horse who can hold a handy position rather than needing soft ground to deliver a sustained late run.

races.name: Haven Handicap

runners_data.name: Zaraquelle
runners_data.note: 332 days off the track is a significant flag for this two-year-old making what is effectively a comeback run; rides hold-up but her handful of runs suggest she stays beyond a mile and Yarmouth's flat track suits, though her four similar-going runs produced just one placed effort and she carries top weight for her OR relative to experience.|
runners_data.comment: Zaraquelle heads our figures at 63, best of this seven-runner field, on the strength of a solid third last time out. She has today's distance in her favour and steps up to first-time tongue-tie, though she remains without a win in her last four starts.

runners_data.name: Divot
runners_data.note: William Knight has sent three of thirteen runners to the frame in the past fortnight which is an active yard signal; this four-year-old has placed at 12f on all three of his standard-ground starts and Yarmouth's galloping straight should play to his staying stamina, making him one of the more credible hold-up threats if he can find a position close enough to Zafaan.|
runners_data.comment: Divot has been competitive in this sequence, placed third or better in three of his last five starts, with both today's trip and going fully proven. Our rating of 60 is backed by a useful speed figure of 61, though he slipped to seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: Zafaan
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter; two wins from eight runs on good ground and a recent win 12 days ago show he is in form, but racing out of his natural longer-trip comfort zone (history is 10f-17f) and his STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects that this trip and positional dynamic are slightly compressed for him.|
runners_data.comment: Zafaan boasts a progressive profile, with two wins in his last five starts including last time out, and both today's trip and going are proven. Fresh off a recent run, our rating of 61 makes him the pick on these figures, a close second of seven.

runners_data.name: Spaceage Love Song
runners_data.note: Michael Bell is operating at a sharp 2/3 T14 clip which is the strongest trainer angle in the race; naturally a hold-up horse — mapped to midfield only because the rear is overcrowded — so the note of STYLE_FIT 0.91 and a sim-going record of 0 wins from 14 on turf tempers enthusiasm, though his one win came over this exact trip on standard ground.|
runners_data.comment: Spaceage Love Song won four starts back but form since has been moderate, with today's trip and going both proven and first-time visor added. Our rating of 53 rates him a fair fifth of seven, with a 105-day absence the biggest concern.

runners_data.name: Sweetstevie
runners_data.note: Flags a worrying ⚠ fade-in-finish pattern backed by form figures of 10-10-9 on fast ground, and his two best efforts came on soft; the STYLE_FIT note and his redistribution from the rear suggest he will struggle to get a natural position in a field stacked with closers, and Patrick Owens has gone 0/6 in the past fortnight.|
runners_data.comment: Sweetstevie's recent form is patchy, with just one placed effort among five starts otherwise ranging from fifth to unplaced, and he remains without a win in that time. Trip and going are both proven, and first-time visor is added, though our rating of 47 is among the lowest.

runners_data.name: Pure Theory
runners_data.note: Stephanie Cassidy sends this mare across for a rare run (0/1 T14) and the form string of 546900 contains a zero last time out; her sim-going record shows two placed efforts from fifteen which is thin evidence, and while she wears a hood (hg:p) that may sharpen her early, she is an out-and-out closer in a race that does not set up for the deepest held-up types.|
runners_data.comment: Pure Theory ran to a fair fourth and fifth earlier in this sequence, and though her last two runs were both unplaced, today's trip and going are proven and first-time cheekpieces are now added. Our rating of 53 puts her a competitive fourth of seven.

runners_data.name: Sunset In Paris
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran whose last five efforts at 10f on any ground read 5-4-9-9-9 — the positional slide is stark; J R Jenkins has sent 0/3 to the frame in 14 days, Jonny Peate takes the ride, and this horse's redistribution from the rear to midfield on the map does not reflect what he will actually do in running — expect him to settle last or near last.|
runners_data.comment: Sunset In Paris has managed nothing better than third in his last five starts, with two ninths mixed in, and remains without a win in that time. Both today's trip and going are proven, and first-time cheekpieces are added, though our rating of 46 is the lowest in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Zafaan is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-strong field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the gates, he is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m2f trip on ground that is riding Good to Firm throughout the day at Yarmouth. The remainder of the field — Zaraquelle, Divot, Spaceage Love Song, Sweetstevie, Pure Theory and Sunset In Paris — are all hold-up or midfield types by nature, meaning Zafaan faces zero early pressure and can set whatever fractions suit him. This race shape is unusually clean: one horse controls the tempo from the front while a cluster of closers must generate their own momentum from off the pace on a flat, galloping track that does not naturally aid late finishers. The field contains more genuine hold-up horses than can realistically be accommodated at the rear simultaneously, with Spaceage Love Song, Sweetstevie, Pure Theory and Sunset In Paris all redistributed from their true style — the horses most likely to actually push forward into midfield contact and apply pressure in the straight are those with the widest current form and most active trainers, namely Spaceage Love Song (Michael Bell, 2/3 T14) and Divot (William Knight, 3/13 T14). The tactical verdict is clear: a lone, uncontested front-runner on a flat course setting a comfortable pace strongly favours horses tracking in second or third who can pounce on Zafaan's lead in the final two furlongs, rather than true deep closers who face an unassisted grind from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zafaan Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zafaan bowls along in front at his own pace and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Zafaan dictates every fraction on a track that suits front-runners when the pace is honest but not brutal, and with no rival willing or able to press him, he simply never faces a searching question until it is too late for the closers. The horses best placed to exploit this shape are those tracking him closely enough to pounce rather than those charging from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third wheel tracks Zafaan through the final bend and storms past in the last furlong.
scenarios.body: Zafaan's moderate pace sets up a race where a horse with energy in reserve sitting just off the leader can produce a sustained challenge on the flat Yarmouth straight; Divot's course-and-distance history and Zaraquelle's hold-up profile suit this dynamic if they manage to position closer than their natural style demands.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a genuine deep closer charges through with a late run.
scenarios.body: For this to materialise the early gallop would need to have been faster than expected and the front two exhausted enough to be caught; the redistributed closers — Spaceage Love Song or Sweetstevie — would need to have secured a viable mid-race position rather than their true rear-of-field berth, making this scenario structurally less likely. Spaceage Love Song's one win came from a prominent-ish position on standard ground, not a true waiting ride, which limits confidence in a pure late-burst scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Zafaan fades sharply turning for home after setting a misleadingly fast early tempo, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Zafaan to have been pressured into a quicker opening half-mile than his form suggests he would set, or for him to simply stop, at which point the race becomes a sprint among tired horses; Pure Theory or Sunset In Paris would need to have been travelling in a prominent enough position to benefit, but their recent form figures and style fit make this a low-probability, high-chaos outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Divot tracks Zafaan directly into second place from the break — if he gets that position he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given his placing record at 12f on comparable ground.

Zafaan's early sectionals are the key variable: if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable clip the race is likely settled before the final furlong, but any sign of him getting caught in a rare battle for the lead would change the entire shape.

Spaceage Love Song's true running style means Kieran Shoemark will need to make a conscious decision to ride more prominently than natural — watch the early running to see if he pushes up or drops back to his instinctive rear-of-field position, as the former is required for his chances to be live.

Sweetstevie's fade-in-finish flag combined with the soft-ground preference makes him one to oppose if the market shortens him — Good to Firm is recorded for this race and his one recent placed run came on soft, so ground conditions actively work against him today.

Zaraquelle's 332-day absence (with jockey change flagged at 317 days) means her fitness and racecourse behaviour after such a long layoff are genuine unknowns — watch her in the paddock and early running for signs of freshness or greenness that could affect the shape of the field behind her.
